headline: Bohm's 10th-inning homer evens Wild Card Series
recap: The Phillies beat the Braves 4-3 in 10 innings to even the NL Wild Card Series at one game apiece. Bryce Harper's RBI single scored Trea Turner in the top of the first for a 1-0 Philadelphia lead, but Matt Olson's RBI single tied it in the bottom half off starter Cristopher Sanchez. Atlanta went ahead in the seventh on Drake Baldwin's RBI double and a Matt Olson sacrifice fly, making it 3-1; Sanchez was charged with all three runs over 6 2/3 innings. Philadelphia answered in the eighth when Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hit back-to-back solo home runs off Dylan Lee to tie it 3-3, then Alec Bohm put the Phillies ahead for good with a solo home run in the top of the 10th off Didier Fuentes, who took the loss. Andrew Painter threw three scoreless innings of relief for the win.

The win pulled Philadelphia even in the best-of-three series after dropping Tuesday's opener 5-3. The Phillies closed the regular season 88-74, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-winning Braves, before reaching the playoffs as a wild card.

Game 3, the decisive game of the series, is today at Truist Park with first pitch at 8:00 p.m. ET. Neither team had announced a starting pitcher as of this writing. DraftKings lists Philadelphia as a slight moneyline favorite at -118, with Atlanta at -102.
